slide_title: Radar Shooting of Positive Target (Enemy plane)

layout.arrangement: Title top-left with a yellow slide-number circle top-right. Below the title, a large bordered table/diagram occupies the left and center of the slide. A narrower right-side panel contains two stacked confusion-matrix tables. The main table has two columns headed Positive and Negative, and two rows labeled Actual and Model Output, with the row labels rotated vertically on the far left.

regions.name: title
regions.content: Radar Shooting of Positive Target (Enemy plane); the word Positive is red, the rest is black

regions.name: main radar diagram
regions.content: Two-column, two-row bordered table with plane icons, colored numbered circles, classification labels, TP/FN/TN/FP labels, and two purple Correctly Classified arrows

regions.name: right confusion matrices
regions.content: Two stacked 2x2 confusion matrices; the upper one uses TP/FN/FP/TN labels and the lower one uses numeric values 18/12/10/60. The caption Confusion Matrix sits between them.

layout.hierarchy: The title is the largest text. The main radar diagram dominates the left side through its size, colored circles, and plane icons. The right-side confusion matrices are smaller supporting visuals. Colored red/green circles and green/yellow matrix cells provide strong visual accents.

visual_elements.description: Main radar-shooting table. Top row headers: Positive in red and Negative in green. Under Positive is an enemy plane icon; under Negative is a friendly plane icon. A red circle labeled 30 sits under Positive and branches down to a red circle labeled 18 and a green circle labeled 12. A green circle labeled 70 sits under Negative and branches down to a green circle labeled 60 and a red circle labeled 10. Bottom row has four aligned columns: Classified as: Positive / Negative / Negative / Positive; And classification is: True / False / True / False; then TP / FN / TN / FP. Purple upward arrows sit beneath TP and TN, each labeled Correctly Classified.

Upper confusion matrix. Header Predicted as spans columns P and N. Left row label Actual spans rows P and N. Cells: row P = TP with green fill, FN with yellow fill; row N = FP with yellow fill, TN with green fill.

Lower confusion matrix with the same structure as the upper one. Header Predicted as spans P and N; left row label Actual spans P and N. Cells: row P = 18 with green fill, 12 with yellow fill; row N = 10 with yellow fill, 60 with green fill.
Yellow circular slide-number badge containing the black numeral 4.

imagery: Left top cell: gray line-art enemy plane with a skull-and-crossbones marking, placed under the Positive header.
Right top cell: gray/green line-art friendly plane, placed under the Negative header.
typography_notes: Sans-serif, Arial-like. Title is bold and larger than body text; the word Positive in the title is red. Column headers Positive and Negative are colored red and green. Row labels Actual and Model Output are rotated vertically and appear blue. Body text is small and mostly black. TP, FN, TN, FP, P, and N are all-caps. Correctly Classified is purple; Confusion Matrix is blue.
animation_state: No mid-build indicated; all elements are fully visible.
recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to white. 2. Add a title text box at the top-left reading Radar Shooting of Positive Target (Enemy plane); use bold sans-serif about 32pt, black text, but make the word Positive red #C00000. 3. Add a yellow circle at the top-right with a black outline and the black numeral 4 inside. 4. Draw a large bordered rectangle/table from about x=4% to x=68% and y=20% to y=90%. Add a vertical divider near the center and a horizontal divider between the upper Actual row and lower Model Output row. 5. Add rotated left-side row labels Actual and Model Output in blue. 6. In the top row, add column headers Positive in red #C00000 and Negative in green #008000. Place a gray enemy-plane icon with a skull marking under Positive and a gray/green friendly-plane icon under Negative. 7. In the middle band, add a red circle labeled 30 under Positive and a green circle labeled 70 under Negative. Draw connector lines from 30 down-left to a red circle labeled 18 and down-right to a green circle labeled 12. Draw connector lines from 70 down-left to a green circle labeled 60 and down-right to a red circle labeled 10. Use white numerals inside the colored circles. 8. In the bottom row, add four aligned columns: Classified as: Positive, Negative, Negative, Positive; And classification is: True, False, True, False; then TP, FN, TN, FP. Color Positive values red and Negative values green; keep True/False black. 9. Add purple upward arrows beneath the TP and TN columns and label each Correctly Classified in purple #800080. 10. On the right, draw the upper confusion matrix: a 2x2 grid with Predicted as spanning P and N, Actual as the vertical row label, and cells TP/FN/FP/TN. Fill TP and TN green #008000 and FN and FP yellow #FFFF00. 11. Below it, add the blue caption Confusion Matrix. 12. Draw the lower confusion matrix with the same headers and row labels, but fill the cells with 18 and 60 in green and 12 and 10 in yellow.
